title: The category of coherent formal modules is abelian
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Then the category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] is abelian [def-sp-abelian]; the cokernel of a morphism $\alpha=(\alpha_n):(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ is the inverse system $(\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n)_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), part (1), and the description of cokernels in its proof

proof.text: Use closure under finite products of the ambient inverse-system category to obtain finite products in the full subcategory. Preadditivity is inherited termwise from the ambient functor category by Mathlib.

For each arrow, extract the kernel object, inclusion, zero-composite equation, and unique factorization from coherentFormalModule_kernel. Construct a limit KernelFork using Fork.IsLimit.mk' and package these limit cones as HasKernels. The use of choice selects uniquely determined universal factorizations, not arbitrary objects.

Use ambient cokernel closure and Mathlib ObjectProperty machinery to obtain HasCokernels in the full subcategory. Its inclusion preserves cokernels. For each arrow take the canonical cokernel cofork; inclusion followed by evaluation preserves its colimit because evaluation of a functor category preserves colimits. This proves the asserted termwise cokernel clause by isColimitOfPreserves.

Install the canonical coimage-image comparison isomorphism for every arrow. Apply Abelian.ofCoimageImageComparisonIsIso to the inherited preadditive structure, finite products, kernels, and cokernels, and pair its result with the cokernel clause.
